title: Attestable expiring session unlinkability for analytics telemetry
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: Console analytics currently store semi-stable session fingerprints (hashed session_id + device footprint) to join events for debugging and feature usage analytics. Those join keys persist beyond short-term debugging windows, increasing re-identification risk and complicating user deletion requests. We need a solution that preserves short-term joinability for operational debugging and metrics while guaranteeing unlinkability after a configurable retention window and providing an auditable attestation that deletion/unlinkability occurred.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry pipeline emits an expirable unlink token instead of persistent session fingerprints for console events
Unlink tokens are derived from rotating KMS-backed keys and expire automatically after retention window; expired tokens cannot be used to re-link historical events
A compact attestation (signed proof) is generated when a retention window elapses and made available to auditors/customers on request
Deletion flow: customer deletion or manual erase triggers immediate revocation and marks tokens as revoked; downstream analytics honor revocation within 15 minutes
E2E tests and load tests demonstrate less than 5% additional pipeline latency and no more than 2% increase in storage for token metadata
Security review completed and playbook updated (runbook + dashboards)
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting with Analytics, Security, and Infra. Agreement on high-level approach: ephemeral unlink tokens + key rotation + attestation service.
2026-03-02: Prototype generator implemented in telemetry-shims (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-shims/pull/128). Uses HMAC-SHA256 with KMS-wrapped key versions and 7-day TTL by default.
2026-03-05: Benchmarked token generation at 60k events/s on a single instance; acceptable baseline. Added metrics for expiration counts in dev cluster.

2026-03-09: Integration test with analytics ingestion pipeline (kafka consumer) shows join window enforcement works; found race where consumer lag could delay revocation by up to 40 minutes — mitigation plan added (fast-path revocation topic).
decisions: Use KMS-managed symmetric keys with versioned HMACs instead of public key signatures to keep token generation cheap and local to telemetry shims.
Default retention window set to 7 days; product can request longer windows per customer via enterprise contract (requires explicit audit and reason).
Attestation will be a signed digest of token revocation events per customer (compact JSON-LD) and stored for 1 year for compliance teams; content will not contain raw tokens.
Revocation fast-path will publish token IDs to a dedicated low-latency topic consumed by downstream services to accelerate enforcement.
comments: Priya Nair (Security) 2026-03-03: Reviewed prototype; requested threat model update for key compromise and suggested HSM-backed KMS keys only for production.

Morgan Lee (Analytics) 2026-03-06: Noted that some historic dashboards rely on cross-session joins older than 30 days; we should add a migration plan or provide summarized aggregates before tokens expire.
Design review 2026-03-08: UX flagged need to surface ‘unlinkability window’ per project in Console so teams understand retention trade-offs.
Diego Martinez 2026-03-10: Created initial runbook draft and linked PR to telemetry-shims; left TODO to add alerting for token-expiration-backlog.
related_incidents: INC-2026-01-console-debug-leak: During a support investigation we re-identified a user via persistent telemetry keys (lessons: need faster revocation and shorter join windows).
